findings.evidence: Up and down days are told apart only by fill colour: navy #1b365d (上涨) vs grey (下跌), both solid bodies. Their contrast with each other is about 2:1 and in a black-and-white print they are close to the same dark grey. The legend is two colour swatches.
findings.before: Filled navy body = up, filled grey body = down
findings.after: Use the print convention: hollow body (stroke only) for up days, filled for down days, or add a pattern; keep the colour as a second cue.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.1 Use of Color and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast; T-GRAYSCALE.

findings.evidence: dom-794.json: the svg has no role, title or aria-label; the figcaption carries the meaning but is not tied to the graphic, so assistive tech reads axis tick labels ('420 400 380… 3/26 4/1…') as loose text in the HTML/PDF tag tree.
findings.after: <svg role="img" aria-labelledby="fig1-cap">…</svg><figcaption id="fig1-cap">…</figcaption>; mark tick labels aria-hidden.

findings.where: 风险与总结 2x2 grid and verdict rows
findings.evidence: Risk titles (资本开支, 交付疲软, HW3 淘汰, 竞争与关税) and verdict labels (多头核心…新建仓) are styled divs, not headings or a definition list, so the tagged PDF loses the label-to-text relationship.
findings.after: <h3> for risk titles; <dl><dt>多头核心</dt><dd>…</dd></dl> for the verdict rows.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (applies to tagged PDF export too).

strengths: lang="zh-CN" and a descriptive title are set; data tables use real th headers.
Spot-checked contrast: secondary grey #6b6a64 on #f5f4ed is 4.9:1 and the navy accent is 11:1; body is 9.5pt and dense tables 8.5pt, inside the PRN-106 print floors.
not_investigated: Image-free print medium: focus order, keyboard, targets, reflow and motion are not applicable
contrast on real pixels: no background-only render for this medium; spot-checked from DOM colours instead
pagination: capture is a continuous 794px render, so page-break splitting (PRN-109) was not checked
